items.name: Variables & Types
items.desc: Give values meaningful names. Python works out the type for you.

examples.label: Start: save one value
examples.code:
name = 'Asha'
age = 20
print(name, age)

examples.label: Next: use values in a message
examples.code:
name = 'Asha'
score = 92.5
is_passing = score >= 70
print(f'{name}: {score} — passing: {is_passing}')

items.name: Type Casting
items.desc: Convert text input into the type your program needs.

examples.label: Start: convert text to a number
examples.code:
age_text = '20'
age = int(age_text)
print(age + 1)  # 21

examples.label: Next: clean and format input
examples.code:
price_text = ' 19.99 '
price = float(price_text.strip())
print(f'₹{price:.2f}')

items.name: Comments & Docstrings
items.desc: Use comments to explain why; use docstrings to explain reusable code.

examples.label: Start: add a comment
examples.code:
# This stores the number of attempts
attempts = 3

examples.label: Next: document a function
examples.code:
def square(number):
    """Return a number multiplied by itself."""
    return number * number

print(square(4))

items.name: Arithmetic
items.desc: Use operators to calculate totals, averages, remainders, and powers.

examples.label: Start: do basic math
examples.code:
apples = 4
more_apples = 3
print(apples + more_apples)  # 7

examples.label: Next: calculate a bill
examples.code:
price = 499
quantity = 2
tax = price * quantity * 0.18
total = price * quantity + tax
print(round(total, 2))

items.name: Comparison & Logic
items.desc: Comparisons return True or False and can be combined with and, or, and not.

examples.label: Start: compare two values
examples.code:
age = 18
print(age >= 18)  # True

examples.label: Next: combine rules
examples.code:
age = 21
has_ticket = True
can_enter = age >= 18 and has_ticket
print(can_enter)

items.name: If - Elif - Else
items.desc: Choose one path based on conditions. Indentation defines each block.

examples.label: Start: make one decision
Next: grade a score

items.name: Conditional Expression
items.desc: A short one-line choice is useful for simple assignments.

examples.label: Start: choose a label
examples.code:
age = 17
label = 'Adult' if age >= 18 else 'Minor'
print(label)

examples.label: Next: choose a discount
examples.code:
cart_total = 1200
discount = 0.10 if cart_total >= 1000 else 0
print(cart_total * (1 - discount))

items.name: For Loop & Range
items.desc: Repeat once for every item, or a known number of times.

examples.label: Start: repeat three times
examples.code:
for number in range(3):
    print(number)

examples.label: Next: process a list

items.name: While Loop
items.desc: Repeat while a condition stays true; make sure something changes inside the loop.

examples.label: Start: count down
examples.code:
count = 3
while count > 0:
    print(count)
    count -= 1

examples.label: Next: count limited attempts
examples.code:
attempts = 0
while attempts < 3:
    attempts += 1
    print(f'Attempt {attempts}')
print('Finished')

items.name: Break, Continue & Pass
items.desc: Use break to stop, continue to skip one turn, and pass as a temporary placeholder.

examples.label: Start: stop a loop
Next: skip unwanted values

items.name: Lists
items.desc: Lists keep ordered items and can be changed after creation.

examples.label: Start: create and read a list
examples.code:
fruits = ['apple', 'mango', 'banana']
print(fruits[0])  # apple

examples.label: Next: add, remove, and sort
examples.code:
scores = [70, 92, 85]
scores.append(98)
scores.remove(70)
scores.sort()
print(scores)

items.name: Dictionaries
items.desc: Dictionaries store values under meaningful keys.

examples.label: Start: look up a value
examples.code:
student = {'name': 'Ravi', 'age': 19}
print(student['name'])

examples.label: Next: safely read and loop

items.name: Sets
items.desc: Sets store unique values and are useful for removing duplicates or comparing groups.

examples.label: Start: remove duplicates
examples.code:
tags = ['python', 'web', 'python']
unique_tags = set(tags)
print(unique_tags)

examples.label: Next: find shared values

items.name: List Comprehensions
items.desc: Build a new list in one readable line when the transformation is simple.

examples.label: Start: transform every item
examples.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3]
squares = [number ** 2 for number in numbers]
print(squares)

examples.label: Next: transform only matching items
examples.code:
scores = [45, 72, 88, 61]
passing = [score for score in scores if score >= 70]
print(passing)

items.name: Tuples & Unpacking
items.desc: Tuples are ordered values that normally stay unchanged; unpacking gives each value a name.

examples.label: Start: make a tuple
examples.code:
point = (10, 20)
print(point[1])  # 20

examples.label: Next: unpack returned values

items.name: Function Definition
items.desc: Functions group reusable steps. Parameters accept input and return sends a result back.

examples.label: Start: make a reusable action
Next: use a default value

items.name: Flexible Args
items.desc: *args collects extra positional values; **kwargs collects named values.

examples.label: Start: accept many numbers
Next: accept optional details

items.name: Lambda Expressions
items.desc: Lambdas are tiny one-expression functions, especially useful as a sort key.

examples.label: Start: make a small function
examples.code:
double = lambda number: number * 2
print(double(5))

examples.label: Next: sort records by a key
examples.code:
users = [{'name': 'Ravi', 'age': 25}, {'name': 'Asha', 'age': 19}]
by_age = sorted(users, key=lambda user: user['age'])
print(by_age)

items.name: Classes & OOP
items.desc: A class combines related data and behaviour into reusable objects.

examples.label: Start: create an object
Next: add useful behaviour

items.name: Try - Except - Finally
items.desc: Handle expected errors so a program can explain the problem instead of crashing.

examples.label: Start: catch one error
Next: handle success and cleanup

items.name: Raising Exceptions
items.desc: Raise a clear exception when a function receives invalid data.

examples.label: Start: reject an invalid value
Next: validate inside a function

items.name: Reading Files Safely
items.desc: Use with so Python closes a file automatically, even if an error happens.

examples.label: Start: read a text file
examples.code:
with open('notes.txt', encoding='utf-8') as file:
    text = file.read()
print(text)

examples.label: Next: handle a missing file
